overview.description: 28 dominoes is block or draw dominoes with a double-6 set of 28 tiles. Two to five players; 7 tiles each (2-3 players) or 5 (4-5 players). Highest double leads. Match numbers on open ends; doubles placed crosswise. Block: pass if cannot play. Draw: draw from boneyard until you can play. First out wins; or lowest pips if blocked.

history.origins: Domino tiles originated in China in the 12th–13th centuries; the modern 28-tile double-six block and draw games developed in France and spread across Europe and worldwide.
timeline: 12th–13th centuries: Chinese gambling tiles and early domino games appear.
Mid-18th century: Modern 28-tile double-six domino set and simple block/draw games are documented in France and England.
19th century: Dominoes spreads across Europe and becomes a common café and pub game worldwide.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

setup.deck: Double-6 domino set of 28 tiles: each tile has two ends with 0–6 pips; every combination appears once. Used for block and draw games.
setup.dealing: 7 each (2-3 players) or 5 each (4-5); rest boneyard.

rules.objective: Play all tiles first, or have fewest pips if blocked.
rules.gameplay: Match to open ends; doubles crosswise. Block: pass if cannot play. Draw: draw until playable.

strategy.basic: Dump high tiles; block when ahead.
strategy.intermediate: Block ends opponents need; in draw variant draw early to keep options.
strategy.advanced: Force block when you have few pips; leave awkward ends.
tips: Agree block vs draw before play.

list.name: Block dominoes
list.description: Standard blocking game with a double-six set: each player draws an initial hand, plays matching tiles to the open ends, and passes when unable to play; the winner is first to play all tiles or the player with the lowest pip total when the game is blocked.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Block dominoes uses the same base engine configuration; the difference is that players simply pass instead of drawing when they cannot play.

list.name: Draw dominoes
list.description: Draw variant using the same double-six set: when a player cannot play they must draw from the boneyard until they find a playable tile or the stock is empty; scoring still uses the remaining pips in opponents' hands.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Draw dominoes shares the same core engine; drawing from the boneyard is handled by rules, so no variant-specific engine overrides are required.

difficulty.hard: Plans several turns ahead, tracks remaining tiles, and plays to force blocks while minimizing pip totals.

considerations: Match to open ends; doubles crosswise; block or draw variant.
Winner scores opponents pips or lowest hand if blocked.
